Pattern Legend

Exhibit / Schedule Header
EXHIBIT 10.6 · Exhibit 10.26 · Schedule A		SEC filing exhibit/schedule marker at document root.
ARTICLE (Roman / Arabic)
ARTICLE I — DEFINITIONS · Article 2		Top-level article grouping, often with Roman numerals.
WHEREAS / Recital Opening
WHEREAS · WITNESSETH · RECITALS · NOW, THEREFORE		Recital clause openers — WHEREAS, WITNESSETH, RECITALS, NOW THEREFORE.
ALL CAPS Heading
RECITALS · REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES · DEFINITIONS		Short line in ALL CAPS used as a major heading (≤80 chars, no trailing punctuation).
Section N.N (keyword)
Section 3.1 · SECTION 12 · Section 1.2(a)		Explicit SECTION or Section keyword followed by a dotted number.
Top-Level Number (N.)
1. Definitions · 12. Termination		Single integer followed by period then a capital-letter title.
Subsection (N.N)
1.1 · 2.3.4 Payments		Dotted numeric subsection (two or more parts), with optional capital-letter title.
Roman Paren (i)
(i) · (ii) · (iii) · (iv) · (viii)		Roman numeral parenthetical sub-list — typically the deepest nesting level.
Lower Alpha Paren (a)
(a) · (b) · (c) · (d)		Lowercase lettered parenthetical — most common list style in US contracts.
Upper Alpha Paren (A)
(A) · (B) · (C) · (D)		Uppercase lettered parenthetical — deeper nesting than lowercase (a)(b).
Numeric Paren (1)
(1) · (2) · (15)		Numbered parenthetical list item.
Bare Letter a)
a) · b) · c)		Letter followed by closing parenthesis only (no opening paren).

Findings: Exhibit Header Pattern

36/50 of the sampled contracts start with EXHIBIT N.N or Exhibit N.N. The one exception starts with REDACTED COPY followed by the agreement title — no exhibit number in the contract text itself (it appears in the SEC filename only).

Hierarchy Patterns Found in CUAD Contracts

Contracts show up to 6 nesting levels. The hierarchy is implicit in typography (ALL CAPS, numbered sections, parenthetical letters/romans) since plain-text extraction loses bold/italic/font-size cues from the original PDF.

PatternRegexCurrent coverage in clauses.py
Exhibit header^(?:EXHIBIT|Exhibit|SCHEDULE|Schedule|ANNEX|Annex)\\s+[\\d.\\w]Not in clauses.py — strips SEC exhibit prefix before chunking
ARTICLE (Roman)^(?:ARTICLE|Article)\\s+(?:[IVXLCDM]+|\\d+)clauses.py catches this via SECTION_RE fallback
Section keyword^(?:SECTION|Section)\\s+\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)*(?:\\([a-z]\\))?\\.?\\s+\\Sclauses.py SECTION_RE — works
Top-level N.^\\d+\\.\\s+[A-Z]Not in clauses.py — missed single-integer sections
Subsection N.N^\\d+\\.\\d+Caught by clauses.py SECTION_RE number group \d+(?:\.\d+)*
ALL CAPS headingshort line, upper() == stripped, len ≤ 80clauses.py detects this as section_title with number=None
(a) alpha paren^\\([a-zA-Z]\\)\\s+\\SNot in clauses.py — missed list items
(i) roman paren^\\([ivxlIVXL]+\\)\\s+\\SNot in clauses.py — missed sub-list items
(1) numeric paren^\\(\\d+\\)\\s+\\SNot in clauses.py — missed numeric list items
a) bare letter^[a-z]\\)\\s+\\SNot in clauses.py — missed bare-letter list items
WHEREAS / RECITALS^(?:RECITALS?|WITNESSETH|WHEREAS|NOW,?\\s+THEREFORE)\\bPartially caught as ALL CAPS heading

Tools for Hierarchy Discovery

From fastest/lightest to most accurate:

ToolInstallStrengthWeaknessBest for
regex (current — clauses.py)built-inZero deps, fast, works on plain textMisses inline sections, no indentation depth, no bold/font infoQuick section detection on already-extracted plain text
docling (IBM, 2024)pip install doclingReads PDF/DOCX using font size + bold to assign heading levels. Returns structured Markdown with # / ## / ###.Needs original PDF/DOCX file; slower than regex; heavy depsIf you have original contract PDFs — gold-standard hierarchy extraction
unstructuredpip install unstructuredpartition_text() classifies lines as Title / NarrativeText / ListItem. Works on plain text without regex.NLP heuristics can misfire on dense legal text; no dotted-number awarenessMixed-format corpora where regex breaks; fast prototype without PDFs
pdfplumber / pdfminerpip install pdfplumberExtracts font size, weight, and position per character — definitive heading detection from PDF layoutRequires PDF source; complex column/table layout handlingFont-based heading extraction when PDFs are available
Indentation analysisbuilt-inLeading-whitespace depth is a reliable proxy for nesting in OCR'd contractsInconsistent indentation in many contracts; not semanticSupplementing regex — add indent_level field to SentenceSpan
LLM-based (Claude API)anthropic SDKHandles any format, edge cases, mixed numbering styles; structured output via tool_useExpensive at scale (510 contracts); latency per documentOne-time pre-processing pass to build a canonical section tree per contract

Recommended Next Steps

Short term — enhance clauses.py with the missing patterns above (top-level N., (a), (i), indentation depth). This gives better clause_path breadcrumbs for the hierarchical retriever at zero extra dependencies.

Medium term — run docling or unstructured as a one-time pre-processing pass over the 510 contracts and cache the resulting section trees alongside the existing sentence span JSONL files. This would give heading-level metadata that regex cannot recover from plain text.

Long term — if original PDFs are available, pdfplumber font-size extraction gives definitive heading levels that map directly to clause_path depth without any regex heuristics.
